key_insight: Rear-jet blockage encloses a recirculation zone that enhances momentum exchange through larger mixing scales, diluting the front jet while the shielded rear jet rises higher.
engineering_relevance: Tandem-jet spacing and velocity ratio affect jet penetration and mixing, so designs should account for recirculation-driven momentum loss rather than treat each jet independently.
method: 40 kHz time-resolved PIV across nine spacing–velocity-ratio conditions.
DMD and SPOD to characterize unsteady shear-layer dynamics.
evidence_signal: Across 68 twin-jet cases and 11 single-jet records, front-jet near-field segments were up to 40% shorter, while exchange reached 1.5× the zone peak and 2.8× the area-integrated single-jet reference at r≈7.
watch_item: The mechanism is supported by observational evidence; no growing global mode was detected only within the resolvable frequency band and record length.
paper_title: Tandem jets in crossflow: the enclosed-recirculation momentum exchange and the unsteady shear-layer dynamics
